correctness.rationale: The reciprocal divisor pairs for 2^a p are exactly {2^i,2^(a-i)p} for i=0..a. Exact binary-mask reversal gives a necessary-and-sufficient rational prime completion bounded by 2^(a+1)-1. Two independent standard-library computations exhaust a=1..9: mask/quotient enumeration and dynamic-programming expansion of actual divisor-pair subset sums for every candidate prime. Direct constructed reciprocal-closed witnesses verify p=23 and 179 at a=9.

value.rationale: The 2026 motivating problem studies strongly pseudoperfect structure and number families. For two-prime-support numbers 2^a p, the count of distinct prime completions at a fixed exponent is a canonical exact fiber invariant. The first multiplicity occurs only at exponent 9 and simultaneously exhibits two different structural omission mechanisms: one omitted reciprocal pair (covered by the narrower 2024 paper) and two omitted pairs (not covered there). This first bifurcation is a natural complete classification and boundary of the one-pair theory, not a random slice or a rediscovery of known individual numbers.
